H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
01 PREFACE 
Disclaimer: If you are in a hurry, skip to article 3. 
I wrote this experience as it could help you to prepare the interviews. 
Even I prepared for HILTI by reading past experiences specially of Pankaj 
Khushalani, my senior whose guidance did help me a lot.  
           It was announced in the mid of July that on-campus internship drive will be started earlier this year as       
              compared to previous years. The first company to visit was Morgan Stanley at end of July and thus the  
     internship season started.  
    Hilti visited VJTI for the on-campus placement drive on 1st September,2022. It was the second year that 
Hilti was visiting VJTI for interns hiring. It is one of the few product-based companies 
that visits VJTI and offers a great stipend of 80K per month. We had the PPT talk 
from 4:00-5:00 pm followed by which online test was scheduled at 6:00 pm. 
 
They sent us the test links by 5:45 pm. We had to start the test between 6:00-6:45 
pm. They used Mettl platform to conduct their test. For this, they even sent us a link 
which would take compatibility test of our computer. We had to download a google 
extension which would take the compatibility test (testing of microphone ,camera 
,etc). I was lucky to have an extra laptop with me and I gave test on it since my 
current laptop couldn’t satisfy those compatibility tests.It was already 6:25pm by the 
time I could complete the above compatibility test and I had to start my Online test 
before 6:45pm failing to which I couldn’t appear for the test. This did made me 
panic before the test which one shouldn’t definitely  wish for. So please ensure to 
read the email sent out by the respective companies, take all the necessary steps 
mentioned in the mail so that you are ready to take the online test on time.  
 
 
After 2 interview rejections, not being shortlisted for interviews with 5 companies, I 
thought the worst that could have happened, had happened. I only did what I could; do 
my processes and wait for the results to follow.

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
02 THE PPT 
Platform: Microsoft Teams. 
Attendees: All final and third-year students with CPI 6 or above from all branches. 
The presentation was taken forward by the technical leads at HTSI and gave the 
students an overview of Hilti, their products, what is HTSI, and the internship 
program. 
About: Hilti is a multi-national company based in Liechtenstein that builds and 
markets products used in manufacturing and construction works, which includes 
hardware, services, and software - where HTSI came in. HTSI is the technology center 
for Hilti based in Pune, India that works on developing one of their major products - 
ON!Track Asset Management. 
What I appreciated a lot about the presentation was the HTSI brought in their interns 
which they hired last year from VJTI. Interns shared their experience of working at 
Hilti for two months and it was a good time to listen to our very own seniors. 
Some details that were shared regarding the

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
03 ONLINE TEST 
Participants: All 250+ third-year students who applied for HTSI were shortlisted 
for the online test. 
Platform: Mettl - audio, video, and screen proctored. 
Duration: 90 minutes. 
Structure : There were total of 7 sections. One timed section of 30 minutes for Cognitive Ability. You 
could the rest 6 sections in the remaining 1 hour. Switching between questions was allowed. 
Questions: 
1 Coding question. 
Given a list of numbers indicating the window number and a number indicating 
the window number to be accessed, modify and return the list after applying 
the MRU strategy. 
In order to implement the Windows screen switch shortcut (WIN + TAB), we need to 
use a Most Recently Used (MRU) strategy which brings the recently accessed window 
to the front. However, the question was quite long and many got confused while 
perceiving the question. 
Example: 
input list - [5, 2, 3, 4, 1], window number to be accessed - 2 
output list - [2, 5, 3, 4, 1] 
Here, as Google Chrome is being accessed at the moment, the next time we use 
WIN + TAB, it will appear at the front of the list. 
 The question was pretty easy but I did waste my 25 minutes as I couldn’t understand it     
properly and the timer on the screen kept on adding extra pressure. 
There were 10 test cases – 7 sample test cases, 2 necessary cases and 1 Edge case as 
listed on Mettl. I couldn’t solve 1 necessary case and 1 Edge case. Now, since I had already 
wasted 25mins on this question, I preferred to  move on to solve other remaining sections and 
come back to this section at the end if time permits. 
There were ample choices for the preferred programming language for the 
question; I had used JAVA8. 
There was a pool of questions and few students had slightly tougher questions.

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
30 questions on Cognitive Ability (timed section - 30 minutes limit). 
These were basic logical reasoning questions with 7-8 mathematical 
reasoning questions towards the end. You can practice these on 
indiabix.com. 
This was the last section I had attempted. There were questions based on 
graphical analysis, reading comprehension which were pretty lengthy to 
read, blood relations, and so on. You have to be really quick in solving this 
questions. I didn’t have time to understand the last six questions(they were 
based on graphical analysis). Since there was no negative marking for wrong 
answers, I did guess work and marked the answers. 
(Tip: Never leave any question unattended because that won’t help you 
anyways. Just mark it and move onto next question) 
6 questions on Data Structures. 
These were some good questions on the usually asked interview questions such 
as number of comparisons while finding an element in array using binary search, 
linked list, creating BST, and contiguous memory allocation of arrays. 
I was able to solve almost all  the questions. 
5 questions on Database Management Systems. 
This part was majorly theoretical. They gave us definitions and asked us 
to identify what kind of key is this called, some questions on inbuilt string 
functions in SQL, and so on. 
6 questions on Networking. 
Questions on the OSI model, transport layer were asked which are the most 
commonly asked topics in interviews. 
There was one question wherein we were given IP address and netmask and we had to 
calculate binary format for it. 
7 questions on Object-Oriented Programming. 
Questions on composition, aggregation were asked based on OOD 
 Java questions were asked based on OOP .This section  was majorly 
theoretical.  
6 questions on Operating Systems. 
Questions were asked on demand paging, threads, memory partitioning, etc.

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
The questions were majorly easy and theoretical based (except for coding section and cognitive ability 
which was purely  application based). 
You really have to manage your time well inorder to complete the test on a good note. 
 
 
The shortlist for the interview was declared on the same day at around 9:30 pm since 
we were having our interviews just the following day. Out of 250+students, only 26 were 
shortlisted for technical interviews and I was fortunate enough to be one of them. 
 
The interviews were scheduled on 2nd September,2022 from 10:45 am to 5:30 pm.

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
04 INTERVIEW   1 
Technical Interview (20 minutes) 
Slot Allotted: 11:30 am-12:15 pm 
Actual Interview: 11:40 am-12:00 pm 
My interview was scheduled for 11:30 AM. From the online test and the PPT, I had gotten 
a fair idea that Java will be tested for sure along with DBMS. So, I revised  multithreading 
,read various articles on most frequently asked Java questions in interview along with 
several SQL queries to prepare for the interview. 
 
 
      Four students were assigned the same time slot and there was a common meet link for everyone.     
       They  would  then assign us breakout rooms where we would be interviewed by the respective panel. 
I joined the Microsoft Teams meeting at 11:25 AM (It’s always a good practice to join 
the interview 5 minutes before the allotted time). I had to wait till 11:35 AM in waiting 
room ,after that I  was cordially greeted by their HR who was really sweet (he was the 
one who had PPT talk with us yesterday). I was assigned to a breakout room at 11:40 
AM. 
There were 2 interviewers, female interviewer and a male interviewer, the cameras were on 
all the time. We both greeted each other. Then female interviewer asked me that she had 
heard  my name for the first time and what did it actually mean. This question really helped 
me in getting comfortable for the interview and reduce nervousness. She then asked, who 
should introduce first, they themselves or me to which I answered I would go first (It really 
helps to create a good impression on interviewers as it depicts that you are confident). Always 
prepare answer for “Tell me about yourself” before hand and practice saying it in front of 
mirror. Then,  they introduced themselves. The female interviewer was alumni of COEP, Pune. 
So we had a small talk on why VJTI over COEP. 
 
Since I mentioned that I had worked with Java and Web Development in my introduction, she 
said that she would like to ask me questions on Java. (Hint: In your introduction, stress on 
those tech stack with which u are very well familiar with and ready to answer any question on 
it. I did mention JAVA 3-4 times in my introduction as I wanted them to ask me questions on it 
because that was one of the  stack that I could answer confidently on. Fortunately, this trick 
worked for me).

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
She asked if I had made any projects using Java. I had made a project using Data Structures 
and OOPs in JAVA.I began with the aim to make this project and then I went on explaining 
each and every minute details of how I made the project, what made me use inheritance and 
polymorphism in project, was it really necessary to use them, what all problems did I face and 
so on.  
Here, I talked about diamond problem in Java and thus not supporting multiple inheritance.  
 
 
She asked me whether it was a solo project or a group project and how much time did I take 
to prepare it. Then I told her that I started the project with a small aim and ended up learning 
a whole new bunch of things (depicts that you are a great learner). They were really 
impressed by me and gave me good compliments. 
 
Then she asked me about garbage collector in Java and said it is totally fine if I couldn’t 
answer it. I was familiar with the question and answered it correctly ,mentioned how it is 
different from destructors in C++. 
 
The male interviewer asked me if I was familiar with Databases to which I answered YES and 
also mentioned how I could  implement it in my project. Again, they were quite impressed. 
 
Then they finally asked me if I had any questions for them. Do ask questions at the end of 
interview ,it showcases that you are really interested in working with the company. 
• 
How has been your experience at HILTI? 
They shared their experience. Then we did have a conversation on whether it is 
necessary to work 18 hours at office(it was a trending topic on LinkedIn at that time) to 
which she replied, work culture at HILTI is too good, you have flexible working hours, 
etc . 
• 
How difficult was it for HILTI to set up business virtually during Covid times? 
 
The interview lasted for 20 mins. Female interviewer had another meeting scheduled at 12:00 
PM, thus she was in hurry to leave the meet and told that she would want me to join HILTI 
and see me in next round. I was really relieved after this statement. Then I talked for 5 mins 
with the male interviewer and the interview ended.  
This was indeed the best interview I had ever given. The interviewers were quite friendly and it didn’t 
seem like an interview rather a casual talk.

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
I was quite surprised after the interview. I wasn’t asked any questions related to Data Structures and 
Algorithms, OS or DBMS(what I was asked was too naïve to be considered as a question).  
Also, I was shocked that my interview lasted only for 20 minutes whereas everyone else’s interview  
went on  till 45 minutes or even an hour.  
I was really in dilemma whether I would be selected or not. Although, there was a slight ray of hope of  
being selected , I began preparing for HR round. I read most famous HR round questions on 
Interviewbit and began revising snapshots taken yesterday at PPT talk. Then, I received an invitation 
for HR round after half an hour. I was asked to join within 5 minutes. 
 
HILTI does focus on HR round and a considerable number of candidates don’t make it through this  
round. So, do prepare well for HR round and don’t take it lightly. I am sure, no one would wish to be 
rejected in HR round considering all the efforts and pain you have put in to reach till here. 
 
 
HR rounds were taken on rolling basis. 15/26 students were selected for  HR round.

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
05 INTERVIEW  2 
HR Interview (20 minutes) 
Time: 12:50 PM-1:10 PM 
This time, I was greeted and congratulated by our very own senior who had joined 
HILTI as FTE this year. We talked for a minute or two and then I was redirected to 
breakout room. 
The female interviewer greeted me and asked me to introduce myself. I introduced 
myself and told her about my achievements and rank holder at MHT-CET to which she 
asked me what is MHT-CET. I explained her well about it.I did mention here about 
mentoring over 14K+ students on Youtube and guiding them to crack MHT-CET to 
which she asked how did u get to know that there were 14K+ students. I mentioned 
that number of views and comments on video helped me to get a rough idea about 
the figure. 
I had mentioned about earning SQL badge on Hackerrank on my resume .So, she 
asked me what Hackerrank exactly is. I explained her about Hackerrank. 
 Next she asked that my profile is filled with just coding and technology related stuff, 
so what do I do in extra-curricular? 
• I started explaining my Interschool competition achievements to her following 
which she said lets not talk about school, it’s too old . Tell me something that u 
do for extra-curricular in college.  
• I stated that first year of college being online,we couldn’t get chance to 
participate in offline events. In second year, I played volleyball for Computer 
Science Branch team at sports event. Though we couldn’t win the game, we 
gave a tough fight to opponent and lost by a minimal margin. (Note: Always 
saying that you won the game doesn’t work, saying that you lost the game but 
you competed hard also works sometimes and it worked for me). 
• Then I mentioned that in my free-time, I read books. I have read “The ATOMIC 
HABITS”, currently I am reading “RICH DAD POOR DAD” and I am planning to 
read “DO EPIC SHIT”(the then hot-selling book in India).

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
Follow-up question: Tell me any two key takeaways from the book “The Atomic 
Habits”. 
• I explained her takeaways pretty well. 
Then she asked me a situation based question. These questions are pretty common in 
HR round. 
• Assume that we are selling a product to customer, customer has his own ideas 
and he wants those ideas in the product. The catch is his ideas are impractical 
and could harm the product. But the customer being arrogant, isn’t able to 
understand this thing and is continuously demanding for it. You have tried all 
possible ways to make him understand but in vain. What would you do in this 
situation if you were employee of that product based company? 
➢ I started off with a naïve solution. First, what we could easily do is let go 
off that customer as he isn’t willing to understand the problem. By doing 
so,we will loose our customer which will result in loss of company as less 
revenue would be generated and it will also have negative effect on the 
image of the company.So this solution should be avoided. 
➢ This was the final solution I gave her. What we could do is tell him for 
time being that you are right. We will implement your idea on a dummy 
product and see its results. Sometimes practical experience is more 
important than theoretical experience. When his idea on dummy product 
would lead to negative outcome, he would easily understand that he was 
wrong. In this way, he wouldn’t feel that his ego is hurt and we would be 
able to retain our customers. 
Then she asked me another famous yet important question: Why do you want to join 
HILTI? 
• Always answer this question in such a way that interviewer should be convinced 
that you can add value to the company. I tried to explain her using example 
from my recent project. I told her that my project helped me to take feedback 
from my clients for whom I developed it, then I thought on feedback whether it 
was a positive or negative feedback and if it was possible to come up with a 
solution for that problem. As I worked on that feedback and implemented new 
feature on my project, I could convince her that HILTI being product-based 
company, its necessary for employees to take timely feedbacks from clients and

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
thus, I could be an asset for the company. 
• Also, I mentioned that from previous experiences of our seniors, I got to know 
HILTI showcases a lot of trust in their employees. I really loved this thing about 
HILTI .Nowadays, it is difficult to find such companies who trust their 
employees. Thus, I would love to work for HILTI. This question went pretty 
well. 
Finally, she asked me if I had any questions for her. I simply asked just one question: 
• How has been the work culture at HILTI? 
On listening this question, she began laughing and said why is everyone asking 
me the same question since morning? Why are you all so interested in knowing 
my work culture at HILTI? Well, both of us were laughing at this point. Then, 
she politely told me about her work experience and culture at HILTI. 
Thus, my interview ended. It lasted for 20 mins. On talking to my friends, I got to 
know that their interview lasted for 30-40 minutes. Hence, again I went into the same 
state of emotions just as Round 1, infact a little more worried this time because after 
reaching last round and facing so many rejections earlier, I didn’t want to be rejected 
this time atleast. But, all I could do is just wait for the results. So, to avoid a plethora 
of negative thoughts of being rejected, I simply slept at afternoon.  
 
 Results were announced at 7:00 PM. Out of 15 students, 7 students were selected 
and I was fortunate enough to be one of them. We were informed that there is a short 
meeting scheduled at 7:20 PM with the HR. Hence, I texted TPO CR, do we have to 
again wear formals or Tee would be fine to which he laughed and said that it was just 
an informal meet to congratulate us.HR asked us how the entire day had been and all 
7 of us could be seen smiling celebrating the success .The following week, we were 
introduced to the General Manager of HILTI.

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
06 Important Tips 
 
Here are few important tips based on what I learned from my rejections in interviews of previous 
companies and what made me get into HILTI. 
 
Kindly keep these things in your mind while appearing for interviews, because I don’t want anyone of 
you to repeat the same mistakes that I made during my interviews.  
 
DONT’S: 
➢ If the name of company is some acronym, do find the full form of that acronym before sitting for 
the interviews. I was asked the full form in one of the interviews which I couldn’t answer 
unfortunately. Also, say the acronym the way it is said. Eg: If the company name is A.B.C, don’t 
just simply say ABC, instead say A-B-C. I did this mistake in the interview wherein the interviewer 
got angry and asked me,  do u know that ABC in Greek language means a PIG. So, never ever  
call our company as pig.  
 
➢ If the interviewer asks you to pick up some topic on which he could ask the questions, kindly 
name the topic and don’t simply say “You can ask anything”. I did the same mistake. So he  
ended up asking what is Azure. I began answering it smoothly following which he said, ”Forget 
Azure, tell me what ERP is?”  I couldn’t answer this. Thus he told me that never ever say 
 “Ask me anything”, it simply means that you know everything which gives him liberty to ask  
you any questions. He then again asked me to pick up a topic and I picked DSA. Here again, it 
could be a double edged sword: 
  
• 
If the you pick up the topic that u know thoroughly well and interviewer is kind enough to ask  
you questions on the same topic, then well and good. 
• 
But, if the interviewer is smart enough thinking that since you already know this topic ,so let’s 
 test you on some other topic, then you might be in trouble. So, think before answering and 
 trust your preparation. 
➢ Don’t ever take HR round lightly. Prepare well for it. Read the famous HR interview questions on 
internet, try to correlate it with your projects or experience and prepare an answer before hand so 
that you won’t have to think on that question during the interview. HR round is generally the last 
round in interview and you would definitely not wish to be get rejected here. 
 
➢ Never mention those projects or tech stack on your resume on which you haven’t worked  
recently in the past. You might have forget that stack and if interviewer asks you questions 
regarding it, you might end up in trouble. 
 
➢ Always choose that project on which you can be able to answer follow-up questions. I mentioned 
about OOPs in my project in one of my interviews at other company and then they asked me to 
design an entire Railway Train. Since  we weren’t taught Object Oriented Design, I was stuck  
there and couldn’t answer the question.

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
 
 
  DO’S: 
 
➢ Kindly check the compatibility of your laptop/PC before appearing for the test (tests are proctored, 
so check if camera, microphone ,etc is working well or not).  
 
➢ Always pay attention to PPT talk that takes place before Online Test and if possible, try to take 
snapshots of it which will help you in preparing for HR round process. 
➢ Always have projects(those mentioned on resume) ready to run on your laptop. You never 
know,when an interviewer may ask you to show the demo of your project and explain. I was asked 
to show my project at HILTI’s interview but since I was using another laptop for interview, I  
explained the situation and they said its fine. It might not be the same case everytime . So be on 
safer side and have your projects ready to run. 
 
➢ Always, try to explain your projects or any other answer to interviewer using hand gestures. It  
does help a lot in boosting your confidence and create a good impact on interviewer. I followed 
 and it worked for me. 
 
➢ Have patience while you are appearing for interview. It may happen that you may have to wait in 
waiting room for 5-10 minutes but its fine. I got a compliment from my interviewer that it was  
good to see that I am patient and if possible, keep your camera on while waiting and have a  
smile on your face rather than making expressions for making you wait. Join the meeting  
5 minutes early than the allotted time. 
•   You can definitely reach me out at  chaityavora20@gmail.com  or LinkedIn. I would be glad to 
help you.

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
07 THE PREP 
Data Structures & Algorithms 
o I practiced 450 DSA sheet by Love Babbar. It’s a wonderful sheet if you are a 
 beginner and it has variety of questions based from easy, medium to difficult level.  
o In case, you don’t have much time for preparation, you can definitely try SDE sheet by 
Striver. It consists around 180-190 questions and you may find many overlapping 
problems in SDE sheet as well as 450 DSA sheet. 
o I used to solve LeetCode Daily Challenge every single day. Do it religiously without 
missing out a day or procrastinating it. It may seem a difficult task at first, but trust me, 
these efforts put in by you will definitely you in your career and crack many companies. 
o For learning Recursion ,Binary Trees, Binary Search Trees, Tries ,Dynamic 
Programming, Graphs, I watched TakeUForward channel taught by Striver (Raja 
Vikramaditya).You can also refer my Notes(prepared by watching TakeUForward 
channel) just in case you want. 
o Whatever topics you learn, try to make their notes. It will definitely help you at the last 
moment when you won’t have time to go through each topic again. 
o Timely revision is the ultimate key to success. It doesn’t matter if you solve 400+ 
problems and forget the logic behind solving the first problem, it would be of no use. 
There would be no difference between you and the guy not practicing at all. So do keep 
revising topics at certain intervals of time. 
o Don’t focus on solving more number of problems, instead try to understand the logic 
behind it. Remember, Quality matters not the quantity. 
o LeetCode organizes Weekly Contest every Sunday at 8:00 AM and BiWeekly Contest 
once in two weeks(Saturday) at 8:00 PM. Try giving these contests as you will gain 
interview experience while solving the problems because the timer on the screen does 
create extra pressure during interviews.You will learn time management as well by 
practicing these contests. 
• Object Oriented Programming 
o I referred OOPs sheet by Love Babbar. It’s a good sheet to learn from and covers all 
the important topics. 
o Also, learn how to implement OOPs in your coding language. You may be asked to 
demonstrate it in your interview.

H T S I | H I L T I T E C H N O L O G Y S O L U T I O N S I N D I A 
 
Operating Systems 
Simply watch the entire OS playlist of Gate Smashers and make notes! 
Can't go without GFG commonly asked 
questions. Tips - 
Virtual memory is extremely important along with process 
synchronization techniques such as mutex locks, semaphores. 
If you know Java, try to practice multithreading in Java. 
Multitasking vs. multiprogramming, processor vs. core, parallelism vs. 
concurrency, thread vs. process are common comparison questions so do 
them well. 
Database Management Systems 
Watched Sanchit Jain's playlist on DBMS. 
If beginner, practice SQL on HackerRank and then move to LeetCode. 
This covers all the important SQL queries. 
For indexing, refer to Abdul Bari's video in particular. 
Not much theory is asked except for ACID properties and normalization. For 
other theory questions, refer to GFG interview questions. 
Tips - 
If you have used a database in any of your projects, be well prepared to 
talk about the schema and queries done on the database. 
You should also be able to justify the choice of the database made for the 
project. 
Don't be worried about vendor-specific SQL clauses such as DENSE_RANK 
while practicing SQL queries. There are hundreds of SQL clauses and you 
are not supposed to know all. 
Computer Networks 
Study in brief about each layer of the OSI model, focus on network and 
transport layers. 
Study TCP, UDP, and the differences between them along with IP. 
Only if you have enough time, go through IP addressing from Gate Smashers, 
3.1 to 3.13. 
Last Minute Notes on CN from GFG. 
JAVA 
Before interview, refer to FAQ interview questions asked in JAVA 
HILTI does ask many questions on JAVA and be prepared to answer them. 
 
• 
Have faith in your preparation and most importantly have faith in yourself.  
Good Luck!!
